title: What Had Happened in Surrey
question: Today, can the narrator (grey eyes, water-soaked charcoal-grey worsted trousers) and the curate (Rather large pale blue eyes, black clerical waistcoat) survive long enough to witness the batteries fall?
light: violet lightning from the west, black shadows
palette: storm black, blood-red glow, green fire, velvet-black vapour, blue night

st_georges_battery.described: A pine-wooded Surrey hill at sunset occupies the picture. Violet lightning from the west strikes the pine crest and throws black shadows across rough heather. Field guns stand in a row through the centre and right, limbers and ammunition waggons wait beyond them, and smoke rises behind the crest. The artilleryman works beside the nearest gun. Martian machines occupy the distant southern slope beyond the trees. Burning pine trunks mark the far horizon, while orange sunset light catches the gun barrels and scattered shell sparks. Low firelight from the burning gun line ahead. The western sky carries the fading light behind the smoke.
st_georges_battery.geometry: The heather covers the bottom edge at medium size. The nearest gun stands at the left edge in medium size. The artilleryman occupies the lower centre at medium size. The remaining guns run toward the right edge at full size. Pine trunks frame both side edges. The smoke column rises from the far centre to the upper edge. The Martian machines stand beyond the gun line at wide size.
st_georges_battery.crowd: one distant gunner works beside the limber; pine branches stir in the wind
st_georges_battery.ambience: wind in pine needles, distant guns, ammunition wagons creaking

halliford_ditch.described: A straight country road runs north through Upper Halliford between high hawthorn hedges. Moonlight from the east touches the road and violet lightning from the west throws black shadows into a broad ditch along the right edge. Dewy nettles and brambles fill the ditch. Flat grass meadows stretch beyond the hedge beneath milky mist. The narrator and curate travel along the road. Martian machines rise across the fields, their dark bodies above the mist. A slender moon, stars, and a ruddy afterglow occupy the upper sky. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT.
halliford_ditch.route: road bend to ditch and hedge
halliford_ditch.geometry: The gravel road begins at the bottom centre and reaches the far centre. The broad ditch fills the right edge at medium size. The near hawthorn hedge crosses the lower left edge. A second hedge frames the left side. The mist covers the middle distance at wide size. The Martian machines stand at the far centre and far right. The moon and stars occupy the upper edge.
halliford_ditch.crowd: one distant battery observer watches from the meadow edge; mist drifts over the grass
halliford_ditch.ambience: wind through hawthorn, wet grass, distant Martian calls

halliford_window.described: A deserted square brick house stands beside the road at Upper Halliford. Starlight from the east enters through the upper window and falls across the landing; searchlights from the east cross the upper window, while violet lightning from the west throws black shadows across the landing. The house has dark red brick walls, a slate roof, white sash windows, a small garden, and a bay window facing the road. Inside, the upper landing frames distant hills and black smoke banks. The narrator and curate watch from the house. Searchlights cross Richmond Hill and Kingston Hill, while red glow and a green meteor mark the night. Starlight falls in from the upper sky beside the window. Grey daylight through the LEFT window.
halliford_window.geometry: The road crosses the bottom edge outside the house. The garden occupies the lower foreground at full size. The brick facade fills the left and right edges at medium size. The bay window stands at the centre in medium size. The upper landing window occupies the far centre. Searchlights sweep across the upper edge, and black smoke banks cover the far valley at wide size.
halliford_window.crowd: one distant watcher stands near the road; searchlight beams sweep across the hills
halliford_window.ambience: window rattles, distant siege guns, house timbers settling

street_cobham_spire.described: A grey stone church spire rises above Street Cobham. Sunlight from the east catches the weathercock and violet lightning from the west throws black shadows across the parapet. The narrow stone parapet occupies the foreground. Beneath it, heavy black vapour covers the village and valley. Red roofs, green trees, barns, gates, and upper storeys rise through the vapour toward distant hills. The church spire offers a high view over the country. Blue daylight occupies the upper sky, while the vapour folds across the lower village. Sunlit roofs punctuate the dark vapour beneath the clear sky.
street_cobham_spire.geometry: The stone parapet fills the bottom edge at close size. The weathercock stands at the upper left edge in close size. Black vapour covers the lower half at wide size. Red roofs and green trees puncture the centre. Barns and gates appear along the right edge at medium size. Distant hills form a band across the upper edge. The blue sky occupies the remaining upper frame.
street_cobham_spire.crowd: one distant roof watcher stands above the vapour; vapour folds across the village valley
street_cobham_spire.ambience: high wind, distant village bells, vapour flowing below

esher_battery.described: A grass hill near Esher holds a British field battery at twilight. A westward fire in the valley throws red light across the hill, and violet lightning from the west throws black shadows across the earth bank. Field guns stand behind the bank, ammunition lies beside the wheels, limbers and horses occupy the rear, and white hospital tents mark the far edge. The artilleryman watches the valley. A towering cone of black vapour advances from the opposite fields, folding upward and spreading across the twilight. Smoke and shell dust veil the distant trees. Fire from the west glints along the gun barrels and tent ropes.
esher_battery.route: gun line to hospital tents and valley
esher_battery.geometry: The earth bank crosses the lower third from left edge to right edge. The nearest field gun stands at the lower left in medium size. The artilleryman occupies the lower centre. Ammunition cases fill the lower right. Limbers and horses stand behind the guns at medium size. Hospital tents mark the far right. The black vapour cone rises across the upper valley.
esher_battery.crowd: two civilian spectators watch beside the hospital tents; black vapour folds over the grass hill
esher_battery.ambience: wind over grass, distant gunfire, horses stamping

richmond_street.described: A steep Richmond street descends between Georgian brick houses before dawn. Grey dawn from the east touches the upper windows while violet lightning from the west throws black shadows across the paving. Gas lamps line the street, their metal posts rising above heavy black vapour. The vapour fills the lower roadway and flows toward the river. Brick houses frame both sides. Upper windows and chimneys stand above the vapour against a grey sky. A faint red glow marks the far end, while the nearest lamp anchors the foreground. Dawn light rests on the roofline above the smoke.
richmond_street.geometry: Brick houses fill both side edges at medium size. The nearest gas lamp stands at the left foreground in medium size. The black vapour occupies the lower centre from bottom edge to middle distance. Doorsteps and railings line the right edge. Upper windows form rows along both sides. The riverward street recedes to the far centre beneath the grey sky.
richmond_street.crowd: one distant Londoner climbs the upper pavement at a walking pace; vapour pours downhill between the houses
richmond_street.ambience: wind between brick houses, distant bells, vapour rushing along stone

hurrying on some operation that disengaged huge volumes of green smoke
shots.why: The offensive has resumed, and the narrator's world now measures danger by the smoke rising from the pit.

source: three certainly came out about eight o’clock
made their way through Byfleet and Pyrford towards Ripley and Weybridge
shots.why: The first human defence fires early, showing the narrator that preparation has become panic.

shots.frame: A shell-lit pine slope fills the frame: one fallen Martian (two immense dark eyes, bare oily brown-grey skin) occupies the centre, the artilleryman stands at the lower right, pine trunks frame both side edges, shell sparks cross the lower edge, and smoke reaches the upper edge.

sounds.sound: artillery shells bursting around a metal fighting machine

source: The shells flashed all round him
advance a few paces, stagger, and go down
shots.why: The guns can still knock down one machine, but the exposed battery has become the target.

shots.frame: The artilleryman (dark brown eyes, dark blue serge frock jacket) stands at the centre beside the gun line, a Martian rises at the far centre beyond the pine trunks, and ammunition cases fill the lower edge beneath the red fire glow. The ammunition blew up
the pine trees all about the guns flashed into fire

shots.changed: three machines regroup beside smoking guns
shots.crowd: one distant scout watches from the pine edge; smoke streams between the trunks

the three sentinels were joined by four other Martians

advance a few paces, stagger, and go down

apparently engaged in the repair of his support

shots.frame: Two black fighting machines cross a milky field mist while the narrator (grey eyes, water-soaked charcoal-grey worsted trousers) and the curate (Rather large pale blue eyes, black clerical waistcoat) approach along the road. The ditch fills the right edge, the road fills the lower left, the machines mark the far horizon, the mist reaches the upper edge, and the moon occupies the top edge.

two of them, black against the western sky, came into sight of myself and the curate

source: the two halted
they took up their positions in the huge crescent about their cylinders in absolute silence

shots.crowd: two civilian spectators watch beside the hospital tents; vapour rolls over the grass hill

sounds.sound: heavy projectile smashing among fields, followed by field guns firing

source: One has to imagine, as well as one may, the fate of those batteries towards Esher
the clumsy projectile whirling over the trees and houses and smashing amid the neighbouring fields
that blackness advancing headlong
men choking and writhing on the ground
shots.why: The final battery is shown as an orderly human effort swallowed by the weapon the narrator has just understood.

shots.frame: Richmond's steep brick street fills the frame, the nearest gas lamp stands at the left edge, black vapour fills the lower roadway, railings line the right edge, upper windows and the grey dawn sky occupy the upper half, and the riverward street reaches the top centre.
shots.motion: The camera rises a measured hand's breadth above the nearest gas lamp across the whole shot; vapour pours between the houses; a grey dawn glow grows above the roofs.
shots.camera: The camera stands at first-floor height beside the nearest brick house.
shots.at_rest: The nearest gas lamp marks the LEFT foreground, black vapour fills the lower street, and upper windows face the riverward slope. Brick houses frame both side edges, railings line the RIGHT pavement, and the grey dawn sky occupies the upper edge.
shots.end: The gas lamp stands above the vapour, brick houses frame the street, and dawn light opens beyond the roofs.
shots.crowd: one distant Londoner climbs the upper pavement at a walking pace; vapour pours downhill between the houses
source: Before dawn the black vapour was pouring through the streets of Richmond
the disintegrating organism of government was, with a last expiring effort, rousing the population of London to the necessity of flight
shots.why: Richmond confirms the answer in a picture: the vapour has passed from battlefield weapon to national catastrophe.

shots.frame: The curate's face (Rather large pale blue eyes, black clerical waistcoat) occupies the centre beside the upper window, black vapour fills the lower view, a red glow lies beyond, the window sash marks the right edge, the dark room frames the left edge, and the ceiling crosses the upper edge.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the curate across the whole shot; the curate faces the window and speaks; vapour flows beneath the upper window.
shots.camera: The camera stands at the upper landing window at a high angle looking down on the curate's face.
shots.at_rest: The curate (Rather large pale blue eyes, black clerical waistcoat) stands beside the window sash at the centre, his head spanning one half of the frame height. Black vapour fills the lower view, red glow rests above the roofs, the sash occupies the right edge, and the dark room frames the left edge.
shots.end: The curate turns from the window, the vapour covers the valley, and vapour flows beneath the upper window.
shots.crowd: one distant watcher stands below the house; vapour flows beneath the upper window
source: Sunday night was the end of the organised opposition to their movements
Before dawn the black vapour was pouring through the streets of Richmond
shots.why: The curate gives the world's answer: the guns have lost, and flight is the remaining human action.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: By nine, green smoke boiled from the Horsell pit while the offensive gathered.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Three machines crossed the evening country, spaced apart, their howls linking the distant roads.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At Ripley, frightened volunteers fired early, scattered on foot, and left the guns exposed.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: One machine crossed the abandoned pieces and reached Painshill Park, where the battery vanished.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The pine battery waited under cover.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Disciplined hands set a deliberate range.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Shells struck around the Martian; its frame buckled, and a second giant rose beyond the trees.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Heat rays swept the battery, turning ammunition and pines into a single burning answer.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Three machines gathered counsel, then one damaged support received patient work beneath its hood.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Four more joined them, and seven black tubes marked a curved frontier across Surrey.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Twelve rockets warned the waiting guns as armed machines crossed the river into mist.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I draw the curate into cover; his fear changes our route from flight to watching.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: What has happened?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Heaven knows!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The nearer machine left the riverbank; across the fields, black hills began to rise.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: From the hedge we watched those vapour summits spread, while distant artillery lost its voice.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The canisters struck earth and opened into heavy vapour, flowing through valleys and ditches.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: High above Street Cobham, a stranded witness saw roofs and trees emerge above the black flow.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At Esher, the waiting order of guns met a cone of vapour, smoke, and falling men.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Before dawn, Richmond filled with black vapour, while organised resistance broke across the country.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: The guns are silent.
